items.x:

Only the Governor is given express (constitutional) discretion (Art. 163(1)-(2)); the President has no constitutional discretion, only situational discretion. The Governor holds office during the President's pleasure (Art. 156) and has no impeachment procedure; the President is impeached (Art. 61), and the CJI and VP have removal procedures.

items.x: The only authority for pardoning a death sentence is the President; the Governor shares the power to suspend and remit, and the powers are not the same.

items.x: Art. 79: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses – so the President is a constituent part of Parliament. The Supreme Court and elections do not 'constitute' it.

items.s: Identify the correct one relating to the tenure of Lok Sabha
o: Cannot be extended under any circumstances
Can be extended by not exceeding one year at a time during the proclamation of emergency
Can be extended by not exceeding 2 years at a time
items.x: During a National Emergency Parliament may extend the Lok Sabha by law for one year at a time; otherwise it has a fixed five-year term.

items.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
items.s: The duration of Lok Sabha may be extended by Parliament by law when a proclamation of emergency is in operation for a period:
o: Not exceeding two years at a time and not extending in any case beyond a period of one year after the proclamation of emergency has ceased to operate
Not exceeding one year at a time and not extending in any case beyond a period of twelve months after the proclamation of emergency has ceased to operate
Not exceeding one year at a time and not extending in any case beyond a period of three months after the proclamation of emergency has ceased to operate
Not exceeding one year at a time and not extending in any case beyond a period of six months after the proclamation of emergency has ceased to operate
items.x: One year at a time, and not beyond six months after the Emergency ceases (Art. 83(2) proviso).

items.s: The Constitutional Amendment Act that increased the seats of Lok Sabha from 525 to 545
items.x: The 31st Amendment Act, 1973 raised the elective strength of the Lok Sabha from 525 to 545. The 21st added Sindhi to the 8th Schedule, the 24th and 25th concerned amendment power and property, the 32nd AP (371D), the 36th Sikkim and the 39th election disputes.

items.x: The 31st Amendment Act, 1973 raised the maximum elective strength of the Lok Sabha from 525 to 545 (later 550 by the Goa, Daman and Diu Reorganisation Act, 1987).

items.s: The Indian Constitution provides that the Rajya Sabha shall consist of not more than ____ members.
items.x: Art. 80 fixes the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha at 250 (238 from States and UTs + 12 nominated); the present strength is 245.

items.s: The States are represented in the Rajya Sabha
o: on the basis of political parties in the State
in proportion to the territory of the State
in proportion to the members of the State Legislatures
in proportion to the population of the State
items.x: Seats are allotted to the States in the Rajya Sabha on the basis of population (Fourth Schedule; UP 31, Tripura 1). The members are elected by the elected MLAs, but the number of seats is not in proportion to the size of the legislature.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I, Assistant Public Relation,
items.s: Which of the following states has the maximum Lok Sabha seats?
items.x: Uttar Pradesh has the most Lok Sabha seats (80), followed by Maharashtra (48) – the printed answer 'Maharashtra' is wrong.

items.s: The State which has the largest number of seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes in Lok Sabha is
items.x: Madhya Pradesh has the most ST-reserved Lok Sabha seats (6), ahead of Odisha and Jharkhand (5 each) and Gujarat (4).

items.s: Which of the following states have the equal representation in Lok Sabha?
items.x: Assam and Jharkhand have 14 Lok Sabha seats each; Haryana 10 / Punjab 13, Kerala 20 / Odisha 21, Bihar 40 / Tamil Nadu 39.

items.s: The following authority is not concerned with the Indian Parliament:
items.x: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses; the PM and Union Cabinet Ministers are members of Parliament and responsible to the Lok Sabha. The Chief Minister belongs to the State executive and legislature, not to Parliament.

items.s: The Rajya Sabha has a life of
items.x: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body, not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every second year. Six years is a member's term, not the House's life.

items.s: Parliament of India consists of
o: Directly elected and nominated members only
Directly elected and indirectly elected members only
Directly elected, indirectly elected and nominated members
items.x: Parliament has directly elected members (Lok Sabha), indirectly elected members (Rajya Sabha) and nominated members (12 in the Rajya Sabha).

items.s: Excluding Uttar Pradesh, the state which sends maximum number of representatives to the Lok Sabha is
items.x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Maharashtra); it is added as option 5.
Maharashtra (48 seats) sends the most Lok Sabha members after Uttar Pradesh (80); of the printed options Bihar has 40, Tamil Nadu 39 and Madhya Pradesh 29 (Bihar had 54 only before its 2000 bifurcation) (printed: no key).

items.s: The fine imposed per day on an ineligible person who sits or votes in any House of the Parliament
items.x: Under Article 104 a person who sits or votes in a House when not qualified, or when disqualified, is liable to a penalty of Rs 500 for each day.

items.s: Which two States in India have 42 seats each in Lok Sabha?
items.x:
undivided AP was split in 2014 — now AP 25 and Telangana 17 seats; West Bengal still 42 (AP Reorganisation Act 2014)
Before 2014 undivided Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal each had 42 Lok Sabha seats (now AP 25, Telangana 17; West Bengal 42).

items.s: Who designed the Parliament House at New Delhi?
items.x: Parliament House (Sansad Bhavan) was designed by Herbert Baker (with Edwin Lutyens), built 1921-27.

items.s: Under Article 79, what is the position of the President with respect to Parliament?
o: An integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House
A member of the Rajya Sabha
A member of the Lok Sabha
items.x: Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses; the President is an integral part of Parliament but not a member of either House.

items.src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer, Royalty Inspector 2020
items.s: Normally how many sessions of the Lok Sabha are held in a year?
items.x: Parliament normally meets in three sessions a year – Budget, Monsoon and Winter; Art. 85 only says six months may not pass between sessions (so at least two).

items.s: The house which is presided over by a non-member of the house
items.x: The Rajya Sabha is presided over by the Vice-President, its ex-officio Chairman, who is not a member of the House; the Speaker, Council Chairman and Assembly Speaker are members of their Houses.

items.src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
items.s: From the given below, under which Article of the Constitution, the Council of State (Rajya Sabha) has a Chairman and Deputy Chairman
items.x: Art. 89 – the Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman and the RS elects a Deputy Chairman; Arts. 108 and 109 are joint sitting and Money Bill procedure, Art. 91 is the Deputy Chairman acting as Chairman.

items.s: Which of the following statements is true about the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
o: He is a member of the Upper House
He is elected by the Rajya Sabha
He is elected by both the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha
He is appointed by the President of India
items.x: The RS Chairman is the Vice-President, elected by an electoral college of members of both Houses (Art. 66); he is not a member of the RS and is not appointed by the President.

items.s: Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy was the speaker of
items.x: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Speaker of the 4th Lok Sabha (1967-69) and again of the 6th (1977), resigning each time.

items.s: First time in the history of the Upper House, four women members were nominated to the panel of Vice Chair Persons. Who was not in the list?
items.x: In July 2023 the RS Chairman nominated P.T. Usha, S. Phangnon Konyak, Fauzia Khan and Sulata Deo to the panel of Vice-Chairpersons – Priyanka Chaturvedi was not among them.

items.s: What is the quorum for Lok Sabha meetings?
items.x: The quorum of either House is one-tenth of its total membership (Art. 100(3)), which for the Lok Sabha is about 55 members.

items.s: The time gap between two sessions of Parliament is not more than:
items.x: Art. 85: not more than six months may pass between two sessions of Parliament (Art. 174 has the same rule for State Legislatures).

items.src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
items.s: The time period between the last sitting of one session of Parliament and the first sitting of the next session shall be less than?
items.x: Art. 85(1): six months shall not intervene between the last sitting of one session of Parliament and the first sitting of the next.

items.s: What is the constitutional quorum for a House of Parliament?
items.x: Under Article 100, the quorum of either House is one-tenth of its total membership.

items.s:
Assertion (A): The gap between two sessions of Parliament cannot exceed six months.
Reason (R): Article 85 implies that Parliament must have at least two sessions in a year.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: Both are true: Article 85 bars a gap of more than six months between sessions, and so Parliament must meet at least twice a year. R is a consequence of A, not its explanation.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
items.s: Who moves the Bills initiated by Government in the Lok Sabha?
items.x: A Government Bill is introduced and piloted by the minister in charge of the subject. The Speaker presides, and the Leader of the House manages business but does not move every Bill.

items.s: The differences between the two houses of parliament are resolved through
o: A joint session of the two houses
A joint committee of the two houses specially constituted for this purpose
A committee under the leadership of Minister for parliamentary Affairs
items.x: A deadlock between the Houses on an ordinary (or financial) Bill is resolved by a joint sitting under Art. 108, presided over by the Speaker.

items.s: How many readings would a Bill go through in a House of the Parliament before it becomes an Act?
items.x: A Bill passes through three readings in each House (introduction/first reading, second reading with clause-by-clause consideration, third reading) before it goes to the other House and the President.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Service
items.s: How many readings would a Bill go through in a House of the Parliament before it becomes an Act?
items.x: A Bill passes through three readings in each House (first, second and third reading) before it becomes an Act on the President's assent.

items.src: APPSC Junior Asst. cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Serv
items.s: In case of deadlock between the two houses of Parliament with regard to a bill, who summons the joint sitting?
items.x: Under Art. 108 the President summons the joint sitting of the two Houses to resolve a deadlock over a Bill (other than a Money or Constitution Amendment Bill); the Speaker only presides.

items.s: Regarding Money Bill, which of the following statements is not correct?
o: A bill shall be deemed to be Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
A money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
A money Bill is concerned with the appropriation of money out of the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
items.x: Art. 110(1) covers the custody of the CFI or Contingency Fund and appropriation out of the CFI; 'appropriation out of the Contingency Fund' is not a Money Bill matter, so (c) is not correct (UPSC key c).
